hints.title: Express everything using one exponential
hints.pitfall: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> is the square of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>, not twice it.

recall.reminder: Rewrite exponential terms in a common base to reveal a hidden polynomial.

hints.title: Keep the order of the two roots
hints.body: Solve the quadratic. Check the roots against the positive range of the exponential, then use its increasing behaviour to identify which belongs to the larger original input.
hints.recap: Ordering a positive exponential orders its inputs when the base exceeds one.
hints.pitfall: Subtracting exponential values does not give the difference of their exponents.
hints.pause: Find and order the permitted substituted roots, then divide the corresponding exponential equations.

recall.reminder: Ordering a positive exponential orders its inputs when the base exceeds one.

hints.title: Turn a quotient into a difference
hints.body: Divide the two exponential equations to obtain one equation involving the difference of the original roots. Take base-ten logarithms and use the power rule to bring that difference down as a multiplier.
hints.recap: The ordered roots determine the order of the quotient and hence the sign of the difference.
hints.pitfall: Subtracting the exponential values does not produce the difference of their exponents.
hints.pause: Derive the exact difference, preserving the factor in the exponent, and express it using base-ten logarithms.

recall.reminder: Logarithms convert powers into products and exponential quotients into exponent differences.

solution:
Put u=22x. The equation becomes u2+12=8u, so (u−6)(u−2)=0. Both roots are positive and therefore valid exponential values.

Since p>q, 22p=6 and 22q=2. Dividing gives 22(p−q)=3, hence p−q=log10(3)2log10(2)=log10(3)log10(4).

Answer E.
knowledgePattern: Quadratic substitution in 2^(2x), then logarithm of a ratio
